# K-Means Clustering

- NVIDIA provides a GPU-accelerated DBSCAN for Spark, shipped in the `spark-rapids-ml` package, which is outside the scope of this course.
- We can, however, use Spark's built-in K-means clustering algorithm.
- For a given \(k\), we can apply k-means to the `iris` dataset using the `ml_kmeans()` function.
- Here, we use the `Petal_Length` and `Petal_Width` features to cluster the data into 3 clusters:

```{r}
set.seed(42)
kmeans_model <- iris_tbl %>%
  ml_kmeans(k = 3, features = c("Petal_Length", "Petal_Width"), seed = 42)

kmeans_model
```

```
## K-means clustering with 3 clusters
##
## Cluster centers:
##   Petal_Length Petal_Width
## 1     1.462000    0.246000
## 2     5.595833    2.037500
## 3     4.269231    1.342308
##
## Within Set Sum of Squared Errors = not computed.
```

## Predict cluster membership

We can use the fitted model to predict cluster membership for each observation in the dataset:

```{r}
predicted <- ml_predict(kmeans_model, iris_tbl) %>%
  collect()

predicted %>%
  count(Species, prediction) %>%
  mutate(prediction = paste0("Cluster_", prediction)) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = prediction, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

| Species    | Cluster_0 | Cluster_1 | Cluster_2 |
| :--------- | :-------- | :-------- | :-------- |
| setosa     | 50        | 0         | 0         |
| versicolor | 0         | 2         | 48        |
| virginica  | 0         | 46        | 4         |

We can see that the species map fairly well to the clusters, although there is some mixing between _versicolor_ and _virginica_.

## Visualize clusters and centres

We can plot the clusters as follows:

```{r}
centres <- kmeans_model$centers # local data.frame with Petal_Length / Petal_Width

ggplot(predicted, aes(Petal_Length, Petal_Width)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = factor(prediction)), size = 2, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_point(data = centres, aes(Petal_Length, Petal_Width), shape = 4, size = 6, stroke = 1.2) +
  scale_color_discrete(name = "Predicted Cluster", labels = paste("Cluster", 0:2)) +
  labs(
    title = "K-Means on Iris (k = 3)",
    subtitle = "Spark ML clusters using Petal Length & Petal Width",
    x = "Petal Length",
    y = "Petal Width"
  )
```

_(注：此处为原幻灯片第 90 页的散点图，展示了各聚类的分布以及中心点标记。)_

Finally, we can use a facet plot to see how the clusters correspond to the species:

```{r}
ggplot(predicted, aes(Petal_Length, Petal_Width)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = factor(prediction)), size = 2, alpha = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~Species, nrow = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Clusters by Species",
    x = "Petal Length",
    y = "Petal Width",
    color = "Predicted Cluster"
  )
```
